channel.title: Japan AI Monitor
channel.description: AI monitoring of Japan's political, economic and security developments

item.title: Tokyo’s record streak of rain comes to an end
item.description: Friday's showers capped the city's longest stretch of rainy days since records began in 1886.

item.title: Japan wants a pharma boom. It needs a new strategy.
item.description: Japan is seeking to make pharmaceuticals a pillar of economic growth and security, requiring innovation and manufacturing capacity.

item.title: Cost pressures and deadlock force Honda to rework India strategy, sources say
item.description: The automaker is partnering with Tata Technologies after its Japanese and Indian managers failed to agree on which suppliers to use for upcoming cars.

item.title: Hokkaido ranked most attractive prefecture for 18th year in a row
item.description: Three cities in Hokkaido — Sapporo, Hakodate and Otaru — also ranked as the top three most attractive municipalities in Japan, a survey found.

item.title: Takaichi mentions Okinawa murder in parliament speech as U.S. military weighs response
item.description: The U.S. side was weighing a period of mourning, among other measures, after a U.S. Marine was arrested in connection with the killing.

item.title: Takaichi lays out ‘proactive fiscal policy’ as new session of parliament begins
item.description: In her policy address, the prime minister said Japan needed further action to turn higher wages and investment into sustained growth.

item.title: Scandal-hit mayor up against six challengers in Yokohama race
item.description: Former Mayor Takeharu Yamanaka is in focus ahead of the Oct. 18 poll, which comes just weeks after his resignation over harassment.

item.title: A first look aboard the shinkansen’s new Supreme Class
item.description: From Oct. 1, select trains running between Tokyo and Hakata will offer the most luxurious way yet to travel on a bullet train.

item.title: Instrument seller works to make disaster-hit town in Miyagi a music hub
item.description: Chiba Prefecture-based Sound House has established a logistics center and showroom in the town of Onagawa, which was struck by the March 2011 tsunami.

item.title: Hiroshima’s rural high schools attract students from across Japan
item.description: Hiroshima's experiment is part of a broader national trend that sees small, rural high schools recruiting students from outside their prefectures.

item.title: Millennium to hire Jera power trader in Japan energy push
item.description: Since being liberalized about a decade ago, Japan's power market has drawn growing interest from domestic and overseas firms as trading expands.

item.title: Thai police rescue two Japanese men believed to have been forced into fraud
item.description: The men are believed to have been forced to take part in fraud at a base in Myanmar.

item.title: Swiss franc, Japanese yen Rise as DeepSeek News Boosts Safe Havens
item.description: The Yen and Swiss Franc were stronger against the dollar as investors sought safe havens after Chinese start-up DeepSeek’s new AI model hit U.S. tech stocks.

item.title: 'Not again': Arrest of US marine for murder reignites protests in Japan's Okinawa
item.description: For many locals on this island, the arrest has brought decades of frustration back to the fore.

item.title: Japan's first mayor to take maternity leave lands on TIME100 Next list
item.description: Shoko Kawata's maternity leave drew mixed reactions in Japan, a country struggling to lift birth rates.

item.title: Japan raises permanent residency fee by 20 times
item.description: The hikes are part of immigration policy changes introduced to manage Japan's growing foreign population.
